docs.title: process-bigraph-lang
docs.text: This is a LSP, CLI and Python package for a domain specific language for process bigraphs.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
process-bigraph-lang defines a domain-specific language (files ending in .pblang) for describing process bigraph composites. A .pblang file is a tree-shaped, verifiable projection of the composite document that process-bigraph (≥ 1.8, with bigraph-schema ≥ 1.6) runs: stores, nodes and edges with their wires, plus the static semantics that compile away (imported or inline interface declarations, parameters, open sites, units, model headers). The design is in the v2 design, its background, the registry and authoring design and the plan.

The repository holds two cooperating projects:

Component Location Language Purpose Langium DSL dsl/ TypeScript The grammar, the checker, the compiler and the decompiler; the language server, the VS Code extension, the browser editor demo and the CLI. Python package process_bigraph_lang/ Python Calls the CLI (compile, decompile, check); describes Python packages and SBML models as headers; compares documents.

Everything the language does is TypeScript. The Python package has no model of a composite: it is the entry to the CLI from Python plus the pieces that have to run in Python.

docs.title: The DSL project (dsl/)
docs.text: dsl/ is a Langium project. Langium generates a parser, AST types and language server infrastructure from the grammar; the project adds its own services and reuses them in every entry point.

docs.title: Grammar and language services (dsl/src/language/)
docs.text:
• pblang.langium is the grammar (language id pblang, files .pblang and .pbl). A module is a flat list of statements: imports, params, meta and options blocks, interface declarations (headers), model declarations (headers and sorts), the composite tree (store, node, process/step edges with config, inputs, outputs, ports, nested composites, shared processes) and emit declarations. See the design's section 2 for the syntax and section 3 for the mapping to the document.
  • generated/ holds the AST types, grammar and module produced by npm run langium:generate. It is gitignored and must be regenerated after every grammar change.
  • process-bigraph-language-module.ts is the dependency-injection module; createProcessBigraphLanguageServices() is the factory every entry point calls.
  • pblang-scope.ts exports every named node (interface and model declarations, imported names), so edges resolve interfaces and model sites resolve headers.
  • v2/ is the language:
  • check.ts is the static checker, registered as a Langium validation (validator.ts): unknown ports, config keys, wires to undeclared stores, wire type mismatches, paths above the root, intervals on steps, unknown components, dynamic ports, untyped stores; writer analysis (additive, overwrite, step arrays); emit paths; units with unit variables (units.ts, mathjs); model sites admitted against sorts. Codes follow the registry design's section 4.
  • headers.ts reads interface and model declarations from manifests and from the text; types.ts is the type expression language (bigraph-schema's string and dict forms, the DSL spelling, a canonical form).
  • model.ts is the object model of a composite, the pivot of compile and decompile: ints are bigint, floats number, dicts Maps in source order; numpy arrays, tuples, params, sidecar references and sites are tagged objects. json.ts is the lossless document codec; yaml.ts the CompositeSpec form.
  • reader.ts classifies a document (or CompositeSpec) into the model; writer.ts writes the model back; printer.ts prints canonical text with sidecar assets for large values, byte-identical to the Python printer it replaced (format.ts reproduces Python's float and json.dumps spellings); bind.ts binds the Langium AST to the model; resolve.ts is what the checker, hover and completion share (which header an edge is declared by, how a path walks the tree).
  • hover.ts and completion.ts are the editor services; graph.ts the wiring graph for viewers; modelheader.ts renders describe-model's JSON.

docs.title: Embedding in another application
docs.text:
dsl/ is also the npm package process-bigraph-lang, staged on npm by every GitHub release at the release's version by .github/workflows/publish-npm.yml through npm's trusted publishing (OIDC, no token) and approved by a maintainer (see dsl/README.md, "Releasing"); npm run pack writes an unreleased build's tarball to dist/. Nothing in src/language/ or src/api.ts touches the file system, so the whole language runs in a browser. The package exports:

Export What it is process-bigraph-lang Pblang: addManifest, addHeader, check, compile (to: "document" \| "spec", strict, force, assets), decompile (text + sidecar assets by path), graph. process-bigraph-lang/worker The language server as a web worker entry (main-browser.ts): diagnostics as you type, hover and completion for an editor such as Monaco through monaco-languageclient. process-bigraph-lang/monarch The Monarch tokenizer (Monaco's "classic" highlighting). process-bigraph-lang/textmate The TextMate grammar (source.pblang), for VS Code-style highlighting. process-bigraph-lang/language-configuration Comments, brackets and auto-closing pairs.

A viewer decompiles a run's document on the main thread with a Pblang session, shows the text in an editor fed by the worker, and draws graph(...). An authoring tool adds the manifests of the environment the document will run in to both: the session through addManifest or setManifests, the worker through the pblang/setManifests notification (SET_MANIFESTS_NOTIFICATION, { manifests }), after which it re-checks every open document. It then compiles the text and submits the document. Manifests come from describe_env.py run inside that environment (registry and authoring, section 1.7). static/ and src/setup*.ts are the reference wiring of Monaco to the worker (npm run dev).

docs.title: The Python package (process_bigraph_lang/v2/)
docs.text:
• api.py is the public API. compile_text / compile_file run cli-native check and then cli-native compile, returning a {"schema", "state"} document or a CompositeSpec mapping (CompileError on errors; strict=True makes warnings fatal; force=True compiles an existing document that relies on defaults the checker flags). decompile runs cli-native decompile and returns canonical .pblang text with its sidecar assets. There is no Python model of a composite and no way to a runnable document that skips the checker: a Python tool that builds composites targets the DSL text.
  • interfaces.py generates interface declarations from a module's step/process classes (describe_module, the publish-time step that imports the classes) as the JSON interface manifest (pbg-interfaces/1, a format shared with other tools; JSON Schema in docs/schemas/) the CLI reads; render_interfaces has the CLI print the .pblang header file. sbml.py describes an SBML model as JSON (pblang-model/0); the CLI renders the model header.
  • check.py wraps cli-native check --json; normalize.py defines document equivalence (equivalent, diff_documents), with types.py as its type parser; langium.py locates and runs the CLI (cli-native, or node dsl/bin/cli.js in a checkout).
  • python -m process_bigraph_lang.v2 compile | decompile | check | diff | describe | describe-model.

docs.title: Native binary: process_bigraph_lang/bin/
docs.text:
This directory holds the cli-native executable the package runs. build.py (also Poetry's build script) runs npm install, npm run langium:generate and npm run build:native in dsl/, then copies dsl/dist/cli-native* here. The wheel includes the binary, so installed users do not need Node or Deno. The wheel is therefore platform-specific: a release builds one per platform (Linux x86_64 and arm64, macOS arm64 and Intel, Windows), re-tagged py3-none-<platform> since the Python is pure, and publishes them to PyPI by trusted publishing (.github/workflows/on-release-main.yml).

Any change to the grammar or TypeScript code only reaches Python after the binary is rebuilt (python build.py, or cd dsl && npm run build:native && cp dist/cli-native ../process_bigraph_lang/bin/).

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
The public Python API of v2: text in, checked documents out; documents in, text out. All of it runs in the DSL CLI (cli-native, TypeScript): parsing, checking, compiling and decompiling. There is no Python model of a composite, so a Python tool that builds composites targets the DSL text, where the result is checked, reviewed and documented (docs/v2/design.md, section 5.3).

  • compile_text / compile_file: .pblang text -> parse -> check -> a process-bigraph {"schema", "state"} document or a CompositeSpec mapping. An error-level finding stops the compile (CompileError carries every finding); warnings and infos come back on the result.
  • decompile: a document or a CompositeSpec mapping -> canonical .pblang text plus sidecar assets.

Documents cross the CLI boundary as JSON in bigraph_schema.json_codec's encoding (numpy arrays tagged), with tuples tagged as {"__tuple__": true, "data": [...]} so that they survive too.

Interface declarations as data: a minimal stage-A describe and the registry the normalizer resolves addresses in.

describe_module imports a Python module once (the publish-time step; authoring never imports) and turns every step/process class it exposes into an InterfaceDecl: the address in portable local:!module.Class form, the config_schema, and the ports obtained by calling inputs()/outputs() with the class standing in for self (ports that depend on an instance are marked dynamic_ports). Types stay in bigraph-schema's own form. The InterfaceRegistry holds declarations and reads and writes the JSON interface manifest (pbg-interfaces/1, a format shared with other tools; the earlier pblang-manifest/0 is still read), which the TypeScript checker, printer and binder consume; render_interfaces has the CLI print the .pblang header file.

describe-model for SBML: a model file's interface as data (see docs/v2/design.md, section 5.6).

describe_sbml reads an SBML file with the standard library's XML parser (no libsbml, no process code) and returns a ModelHeader: the model's time unit, compartments, species (as concentrations unless the species has only substance units) and parameters, each with its value and its units composed from the model's unit definitions in a pint-readable spelling, plus the counts a solver cares about (reactions, events, rules) and the SBML level, version and packages. to_dict is the JSON form (pblang-model/0), which the CLI renders as the .pblang model header (print_model_header).

Equivalence of composite documents modulo representation.

Two documents are equivalent when they realize the same composite. normalize_document rewrites a document into one canonical shape: types are pushed through bigraph-schema (core.access + core.render(defaults=True)), addresses become protocol:data strings, wires become lists, tuples and arrays become lists, runtime keys (instance, _contract, the root global_time) are dropped, and the edge entries of the schema half are folded into the state half. equivalent compares two normalized documents; diff_documents explains a difference.

class CompileError(Exception):
    """The text did not pass the checker; `diagnostics` holds every finding, errors first."""

    def __init__(self, diagnostics: list[Diagnostic]):
        self.diagnostics = diagnostics
        errors = [d for d in diagnostics if d.severity == "error"]
        super().__init__("\n".join(str(d) for d in errors or diagnostics))

docs.title: compile_file(path, *, registry=None, manifests=None, to='document', strict=False, force=False, addresses='import')
docs.text:
Compile a .pblang file; file(...) references resolve next to it. force compiles despite the checker's errors (parse errors still stop it): the escape for documents that rely on defaults the checker flags.

Source code in process_bigraph_lang/v2/api.py 
def compile_file(
    path: str | os.PathLike[str],
    *,
    registry: InterfaceRegistry | None = None,
    manifests: list[Path] | None = None,
    to: Target = "document",
    strict: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
    addresses: AddressForm = "import",
) -> Compiled:
    """
    Compile a `.pblang` file; `file(...)` references resolve next to it. `force` compiles despite the checker's
    errors (parse errors still stop it): the escape for documents that rely on defaults the checker flags.
    """
    source = Path(path).resolve()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        manifest_paths = [*(manifests or []), *registry_manifests(registry, Path(tmp))]
        diagnostics = check_file(source, manifest_paths)
        fatal = set() if force else {"error", "warning"} if strict else {"error"}
        if any(d.severity in fatal for d in diagnostics) or any(d.code == "P001" for d in diagnostics):
            raise CompileError(diagnostics)
        out = Path(tmp) / ("compiled.yaml" if to == "spec" else "compiled.json")
        args = ["compile", str(source), "--to", to, "--out", str(out), "--addresses", addresses]
        args += ["--force"] if force else []
        if manifest_paths:
            args += ["--interfaces", *[str(Path(m).resolve()) for m in manifest_paths]]
        run_cli(*args)
        text = out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if to == "spec":
        import yaml

        return Compiled(yaml.safe_load(text), diagnostics)
    return Compiled(loads(text), diagnostics)

def compile_text(
    text: str,
    *,
    registry: InterfaceRegistry | None = None,
    manifests: list[Path] | None = None,
    to: Target = "document",
    strict: bool = False,
    force: bool = False,
    assets: dict[str, bytes] | None = None,
    addresses: AddressForm = "import",
) -> Compiled:
    """Compile v2 text. `assets` holds the sidecar files `file(...)` references name, by path."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        source = Path(tmp) / "document.pblang"
        source.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
        for name, content in (assets or {}).items():
            target = Path(tmp) / name
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            target.write_bytes(content)
        return compile_file(
            source, registry=registry, manifests=manifests, to=to, strict=strict, force=force, addresses=addresses
        )

docs.text:
Canonical .pblang text (and sidecar assets) for a document or a CompositeSpec mapping (told apart by keys).

Source code in process_bigraph_lang/v2/api.py 
def decompile(
    mapping: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    name: str = "document",
    registry: InterfaceRegistry | None = None,
    manifests: list[Path] | None = None,
) -> Printed:
    """Canonical `.pblang` text (and sidecar assets) for a document or a CompositeSpec mapping (told apart by keys)."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        source = Path(tmp) / f"{name}.json"
        source.write_text(dumps(mapping), encoding="utf-8")
        out = Path(tmp) / f"{name}.pblang"
        args = ["decompile", str(source), "--name", name, "--out", str(out)]
        manifest_paths = [*(manifests or []), *registry_manifests(registry, Path(tmp))]
        if manifest_paths:
            args += ["--interfaces", *[str(Path(m).resolve()) for m in manifest_paths]]
        run_cli(*args)
        printed = Printed(out.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assets_dir = Path(tmp) / f"{name}.assets"
        if assets_dir.is_dir():
            for asset in sorted(assets_dir.iterdir()):
                printed.assets[f"{name}.assets/{asset.name}"] = asset.read_bytes()
        return printed

@dataclass
class InterfaceRegistry:
    """Declarations by address: the manifest the CLI reads, and what the normalizer resolves edges in."""

    decls: list[InterfaceDecl] = field(default_factory=list)

    @classmethod
    def from_modules(cls, *module_names: str) -> InterfaceRegistry:
        registry = cls()
        for module_name in module_names:
            registry.decls.extend(describe_module(module_name))
        return registry

    @classmethod
    def from_manifest(cls, manifest: dict[str, Any]) -> InterfaceRegistry:
        version = manifest.get("schema_version")
        if version not in (None, MANIFEST_VERSION, LEGACY_MANIFEST_VERSION):
            raise ValueError(
                f"unsupported manifest schema_version {version!r}: this reader understands {MANIFEST_VERSION}"
            )
        return cls([_decl_from_manifest(entry) for entry in manifest.get("components", [])])

    def to_manifest(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "$schema": SCHEMA_URL,
            "schema_version": MANIFEST_VERSION,
            "components": [_decl_to_manifest(d) for d in self.decls],
        }

    def lookup(self, address: str) -> InterfaceDecl | None:
        """By exact address; else by unique short name (`local:Name`, or a class re-exported from another module)."""
        wanted = address if ":" in address else f"local:{address}"
        if not wanted.startswith("local:"):
            return None
        exact = [d for d in self.decls if d.address == wanted]
        if exact:
            return exact[0]
        by_name = [d for d in self.decls if d.name == short_name(wanted)]
        return by_name[0] if len(by_name) == 1 else None

    def write_manifest(self, path: Path) -> Path:
        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_manifest(), indent=2, default=str) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return path

def describe_module(module_name: str) -> list[InterfaceDecl]:
    """Declarations for the step/process classes a module defines or re-exports (classes of its own package only)."""
    module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
    is_package = hasattr(module, "__path__")
    decls: list[InterfaceDecl] = []
    for name, cls in inspect.getmembers(module, inspect.isclass):
        if name.startswith("_") or not is_edge_class(cls) or not _belongs_to(cls, module_name, is_package):
            continue
        decls.append(describe_class(cls, module_name, name))
    return decls

def render_interfaces(decls: list[InterfaceDecl], module_name: str) -> str:
    """The `.pblang` header file of a module's declarations, as the CLI prints it."""
    from process_bigraph_lang.v2.langium import run_cli

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        manifest = Path(tmp) / "manifest.json"
        entries = [_decl_to_manifest(d) for d in decls]
        for entry in entries:
            entry["module"] = module_name
        manifest.write_text(json.dumps({"schema_version": MANIFEST_VERSION, "components": entries}, default=str))
        return run_cli("headers", str(manifest)).stdout

def describe_sbml(path: str | Path) -> ModelHeader:
    """The model header of an SBML file."""
    path = Path(path)
    root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    model = root.find("{*}model")
    if model is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no <model> element")
    header = ModelHeader(name=_identifier(path.stem), source=path.name, sbml_id=model.get("id"))
    header.level, header.version = _int(root.get("level")), _int(root.get("version"))
    header.packages = sorted({_package(k) for k in root.attrib if k.endswith(":required")} - {""})
    unit_defs = {d.get("id", ""): _unit_text(d) for d in model.findall("{*}listOfUnitDefinitions/{*}unitDefinition")}

    def units(reference: str | None, default_key: str) -> str | None:
        if reference:
            return unit_defs.get(reference) or _KIND_SYMBOLS.get(reference, reference)
        return unit_defs.get(model.get(f"{default_key}Units") or default_key) or _SBML_DEFAULTS.get(default_key)

    header.time_units = units(None, "time")
    for c in model.findall("{*}listOfCompartments/{*}compartment"):
        dims = _int(c.get("spatialDimensions")) if c.get("spatialDimensions") else 3
        default = {3: "volume", 2: "area", 1: "length"}.get(dims or 3, "volume")
        header.compartments[c.get("id", "")] = Quantity(_float_or_none(c.get("size")), units(c.get("units"), default))
    for sp in model.findall("{*}listOfSpecies/{*}species"):
        name = sp.get("id", "")
        compartment = sp.get("compartment")
        substance = units(sp.get("substanceUnits"), "substance")
        comp_units = (
            header.compartments[compartment].units if compartment in header.compartments else units(None, "volume")
        )
        only_substance = sp.get("hasOnlySubstanceUnits") == "true"
        if only_substance:
            initial, kind, unit_text = _float_or_none(sp.get("initialAmount")), "amount", substance
        elif sp.get("initialConcentration") is not None:
            initial, kind, unit_text = (
                _float_or_none(sp.get("initialConcentration")),
                "concentration",
                _ratio(substance, comp_units),
            )
        else:
            amount = _float_or_none(sp.get("initialAmount"))
            size = header.compartments[compartment].value if compartment in header.compartments else None
            initial = amount / size if amount is not None and size else amount
            kind, unit_text = "concentration", _ratio(substance, comp_units)
            if amount is not None and size:
                header.notes.append(
                    f"species {name}: initial amount {amount:g} converted to concentration by compartment size {size:g}"
                )
        header.species[name] = SpeciesDecl(initial, unit_text, kind, compartment, constant=sp.get("constant") == "true")
    for pr in model.findall("{*}listOfParameters/{*}parameter"):
        header.parameters[pr.get("id", "")] = Quantity(
            _float_or_none(pr.get("value")),
            units(pr.get("units"), "") if pr.get("units") else None,
            pr.get("constant") != "false",
        )
    header.counts = {
        "reactions": len(model.findall("{*}listOfReactions/{*}reaction")),
        "events": len(model.findall("{*}listOfEvents/{*}event")),
        "rules": len(model.findall("{*}listOfRules/*")),
        "function_definitions": len(model.findall("{*}listOfFunctionDefinitions/{*}functionDefinition")),
    }
    return header

docs.title: deep_equal(a, b, *, strict=False, rel_tol=1e-09)
docs.text:
Structural equality that tolerates numpy arrays and float noise.

With strict=False (the normalizer's mode) tuples equal lists and ints equal floats; with strict=True container types and numeric types must match exactly (the v1 parity tests use this).

Source code in process_bigraph_lang/v2/normalize.py 
def deep_equal(a: Any, b: Any, *, strict: bool = False, rel_tol: float = 1e-9) -> bool:
    """
    Structural equality that tolerates numpy arrays and float noise.

    With `strict=False` (the normalizer's mode) tuples equal lists and ints equal floats; with `strict=True`
    container types and numeric types must match exactly (the v1 parity tests use this).
    """
    if isinstance(a, np.ndarray) or isinstance(b, np.ndarray):
        if strict and not (isinstance(a, np.ndarray) and isinstance(b, np.ndarray)):
            return False
        return deep_equal(_to_list(a), _to_list(b), strict=False, rel_tol=rel_tol)
    if isinstance(a, dict) and isinstance(b, dict):
        return set(a) == set(b) and all(deep_equal(a[k], b[k], strict=strict, rel_tol=rel_tol) for k in a)
    if isinstance(a, (list, tuple)) and isinstance(b, (list, tuple)):
        if strict and type(a) is not type(b):
            return False
        return len(a) == len(b) and all(deep_equal(x, y, strict=strict, rel_tol=rel_tol) for x, y in zip(a, b))
    if isinstance(a, bool) or isinstance(b, bool):
        return a is b or (isinstance(a, bool) and isinstance(b, bool) and a == b)
    if _is_number(a) and _is_number(b):
        if strict and (isinstance(a, float) != isinstance(b, float)):
            return False
        return math.isclose(float(a), float(b), rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=0.0)
    return bool(a == b)

Source code in process_bigraph_lang/v2/normalize.py 
def diff_documents(
    a: dict[str, Any], b: dict[str, Any], core: Any, limit: int = 200, registry: InterfaceRegistry | None = None
) -> str:
    """A readable account of how two documents differ after normalization (empty when equivalent)."""
    left, right = normalize_document(a, core, registry), normalize_document(b, core, registry)
    flat_left, flat_right = _flatten(left), _flatten(right)
    lines: list[str] = []
    for key in sorted(set(flat_left) | set(flat_right)):
        if key not in flat_right:
            lines.append(f"- {key}: {_show(flat_left[key])}")
        elif key not in flat_left:
            lines.append(f"+ {key}: {_show(flat_right[key])}")
        elif not deep_equal(flat_left[key], flat_right[key]):
            lines.append(f"~ {key}: {_show(flat_left[key])} -> {_show(flat_right[key])}")
    if len(lines) > limit:
        lines = [*lines[:limit], f"... {len(lines) - limit} more"]
    if not lines and not deep_equal(left, right):
        dump_left = json.dumps(left, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str).splitlines()
        dump_right = json.dumps(right, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str).splitlines()
        lines = list(difflib.unified_diff(dump_left, dump_right, "a", "b", lineterm=""))
    return "\n".join(lines)

def normalize_document(doc: dict[str, Any], core: Any, registry: InterfaceRegistry | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    The canonical shape of a document (see the module docstring). `core` is a bigraph-schema core. With a
    `registry`, an edge's `_inputs`/`_outputs` that merely repeat its interface's face are dropped (process-bigraph
    merges them with `interface()`, so they carry no information).
    """
    table: _EdgeTable = {}
    raw_schema = doc.get("schema") or {}
    schema = _norm_schema(raw_schema, core, (), table)
    state = _norm_state(doc.get("state") or {}, raw_schema, core, (), table, registry)
    options = {k: _canon(doc[k], core) for k in COMPOSITE_OPTION_KEYS if k in doc}
    return {"schema": schema if isinstance(schema, dict) else {}, "state": state, "options": options}

docs.title: Stage two plan: manifests per environment, and authoring in compose-api
docs.text: Status: approved 2026-10-12. Follows the registry and authoring design and the v2 implementation plan; stage one (the read-only composite viewer in compose-api's web app) shipped in compose-api 0.7.12 and 0.7.13.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Stage one shipped: compose-api 0.7.13 shows a submitted .pbg as .pblang text and a wiring graph. Every process shows as "not in the registry" because the browser has no manifests. Stage two (authoring) needs manifests in two places: the main-thread Pblang session (check, compile, graph) and the language-server worker (hover, completion, diagnostics as you type).

Jim asked two things: where manifests are produced (from the registered entries or when environments are built), and where the webapp gets them. Decided 2026-10-12:

  • A manifest is a fact about an environment, not about a package. describe must import the classes inside the image that runs the document. The images differ: registry_env has process-bigraph 1.0.5 (via pbest), while the viva-pde-particle image has 1.8.x and its own core.
  • Producer: compose-api CI, inside each image. A workflow runs a dependency-free describe script in every environment the deployment offers and opens a PR with compose_api/registry/manifests/<env>.json. Each manifest is reviewed like catalog.yaml, works without image owners' cooperation, and is strategy decision 5's phase B first output.
  • viva-pde-particle becomes a registry entry in manifest.yaml, at level tested, with bundle viva-pde-particle. The evidence is its compose-image.yml job-contract and smoke tests. This closes the gap strategy.md records.
  • The webapp gets manifests from the API, same origin: GET /registry/environments and GET /registry/environments/{name}/manifest, through the typed useApi() client. In dev they come from the production API through NUXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE, as today. They are not baked into the static build. Manifests ship in the API image with the other registry files, so a refreshed manifest goes live with the next compose-api release.

docs.title: Facts this rests on (from exploration)
docs.text:
• Environments today:
  • registry_env: a pbest-generated definition, identified by md5. Its image is ghcr.io/biosimulations/registry_env:<hash>. That org package exists but the cluster's pull falls back to a SLURM build.
  • Prebuilt images: PREBUILT_SIMULATORS in kustomize/config/compose-api-rke/api.env, today only viva-pde-particle pinned by digest. Its entrypoint is a bash script that sources /app/docker/shell-hook.sh.
  • Registry of record: compose_api/registry/manifest.yaml plus the generated catalog.yaml. RegistryEntry has module_roots, level and bundles, but no ports. No HTTP route exposes any of it. The legacy /core/processes|steps/list (Postgres, string ports, no write path) stays untouched.
  • The run endpoint: POST /simulation/run?simulator=<name> takes one .pbg file. simulator absent means registry_env.
  • PBL describe (process_bigraph_lang/v2/interfaces.py):
  • It scans only a module's own members, not submodules.
  • It needs bigraph_schema.parse for defaults.
  • _describe in __main__.py always renders headers through the CLI binary.
  • None of that can run inside an arbitrary image.
  • PBL Registry (dsl/src/language/v2/headers.ts) only appends: a second addManifest makes short names ambiguous.
  • PBL worker (dsl/src/language/main-browser.ts) discards the services and registers no custom notifications. WorkspaceRegistry extends Registry, so filling services.validation.HeaderRegistry serves the checker, hover and completion at once.

docs.title: v2 language design
docs.text: Status: design, 2026-10-11. Validated by the round-trip prototype described in the plan. The background is in the research notes; the tooling around the language is in registry and authoring.

docs.title: 0. Framing
docs.text:
.pblang v2 is a tree-shaped, verifiable projection of a process-bigraph composite. Three artifacts share one abstract model:

Artifact Role Produced by *.pblang composite reviewable, checkable, canonical text prompt-guided tools or humans; or decompiled from a document *.pblang interface file generated .d.ts-like declarations per package pblang describe at release time; hand-editable {"schema","state"} document, template, *.composite.yaml what process-bigraph and the workbench run pblang compile

Decisions behind this design:

  1. The syntax is tree-shaped and mirrors the document: nodes nest like the state tree, edges are declared in place, wires use -> relative to the edge's parent, .. goes up.
  2. The DSL is a verifiable target layer, not the only thing an author writes. Diagnostics must be precise and located, the text must be readable for review, and printing must be canonical so generated text is deterministic.
  3. Interfaces come from generated interface files imported like TypeScript .d.ts files.
  4. The DSL interoperates both ways with CompositeSpec *.composite.yaml; param ↔ CompositeSpec parameter ↔ value site with a default.

Non-goals: Python builder logic (engine choice, random placement, probe runs) stays in Python. The DSL captures the result as a ground or template document plus params for the knobs.

docs.title: 1.1 Abstract document
docs.text:
Module    := { name?, docs, imports[], params[], types[], lets[], root: Composite, emitters[], options, meta }
Composite := { nodes: {key -> Node}, options?, bridge?, interface? }
Node      := Store | Subtree | Edge | Replicate
Store     := { type?: TypeExpr, value?: Value | Site, docs }
Subtree   := { type?: TypeExpr, nodes: {key -> Node}, docs }                     // `node x { … }`
Edge      := { kind: process|step|composite|shared|shared_ref, iface?: Ref<Interface>,
               address?: Address | Site(face), config: Value, inputs: Wires, outputs: Wires,
               interval?: Expr, priority?: int, triggers?: [Path], port_overrides?: {inputs, outputs},
               inner?: Composite, bridge?: {inputs, outputs, conduits}, process_id?, extra: {}, docs }
Wires     := {port -> Path | Wires}           Path := [Key | ".." | "*" | Index]
Site      := { sort: TypeExpr | Face | Ref<Interface> | NamedSort, default?: Value }
Replicate := { count: Expr, region: Subtree }                                     // _control: replicate
Param     := { name, type, default?, required, choices?, docs }
Interface := { kind: process|step|adapter|composite, name, address?, config: {key -> {type, default?, docs}},
               inputs: Face, outputs: Face, docs, contract?: {units, min, max, assumptions, refs} }
Face      := { ports: {name -> {type, units?, docs}}, conditional: [{when, ports}], open: bool, delegate?: ConfigKey }
Emitter   := { address, paths: [Path], config }
Options   := { global_time_precision, run_steps_on_init, parallel_*, skip_process_state, contract_strict }

docs.title: 1.2 Denotation
docs.text:
• Store → schema[path] = type, state[path] = value. A site value emits state only (no schema entry; process-bigraph#213).
  • Subtree → a dict in both halves.
  • Edge → the state node {_type, address, config, inputs, outputs, interval?, priority?, _triggers?, _inputs?, _outputs?, …extra}; the schema half gets {"_type": kind} only when there are no port overrides. A composite edge → address: "local:Composite", config: {schema, state, bridge, interface?, options…}.
  • Site by position: value site (store value, config value, param), address site (address of an edge, sorted by the interface face), model site (a node whose sort is a face), named sort, replicate region.
  • Param p has two projections: template mode → a site with _default at the referenced position; spec mode → "${p}" at every reference plus parameters: {p: {type, default, choices, description}}.
  • Emitter → CompositeSpec emitters: or the step node that process_bigraph.emitter.emitter_node_from_declaration builds.
  • Options → top-level document keys, or keys of a nested composite's config.

Deliberately not modelled (stripped by normalization, never printed): instance, _contract, the injected global_time, emitter results stores, serialized dict-form addresses, the legacy composition key, run-specific emitter config injected by the workbench, CompositeSpec id.

docs.title: 1.3 Round-trip equivalence
docs.text:
def normalize(doc, core):
    schema = core.render(core.access(doc.get("schema", {})), defaults=True)
    state = strip(doc["state"])
    # strip: drop runtime keys; address dict -> "proto:data"; wire str -> [str]; tuples/numpy -> lists;
    #        int -> float where the schema says float; sort edge keys;
    #        drop config keys equal to the class default (only when the core resolves the address);
    #        drop _inputs/_outputs equal to interface() of the resolved class
    return {"schema": schema, "state": state, "options": {k: doc[k] for k in OPTION_KEYS if k in doc}}

equivalent(a, b) := normalize(a) == normalize(b)

Three levels, all in the test suite: (1) textual fixpoint, format(parse(text)) == text once a parser exists; (2) semantic, equivalent(compile(decompile(doc)), doc) for every fixture; (3) spec, the yaml round-trip equals the original after key sorting, requires recomputed and id dropped. Nested composites compare recursively on config.state and config.schema using authored documents (saved ones are lossy upstream).

docs.title: 2.1 Lexical
docs.text:
v1 terminals are kept: ID, INT with a leading -, FLOAT needs a ., strings in either quote style, // and /* */ comments. New: /// doc comments attach to the next declaration; ${name} in a string is parameter interpolation.

Keywords: module import as param type struct interface process step adapter composite shared node store let emit options meta every priority at with bridge conduits config inputs outputs ports extra triggers replicate when else of file load true false.

docs.title: 2.2 Grammar sketch
docs.text:
The executable form of the subset the prototype prints is the Lark grammar in process_bigraph_lang/v2/parser.py, verified against every snapshot in tests/fixtures/data/v2/snapshots/. The sketch below is the full target.

Module:        ('module' QualifiedName ';')? TopLevel*;
TopLevel:      Import | Param | TypeDecl | Let | InterfaceDecl | RootComposite | Emit | Options | Meta;
Import:        'import' (QualifiedName ('.' '{' ID (',' ID)* '}')? | STRING ('as' ID)?) ';';
Param:         DOC* 'param' ID ':' TypeExpr ('=' (Value | '?'))? ('choices' '[' Value (',' Value)* ']')? ';';
TypeDecl:      DOC* ('type' ID '=' TypeExpr ';' | 'struct' ID '{' Field* '}');
Field:         DOC* ID ':' TypeExpr ('=' Value)? ';';

TypeExpr:      PrimaryType ('|' PrimaryType)*;                     // union (bigraph `~`)
PrimaryType:   NamedType | GenericType | ArrayType | StructType | LinkType | RawType;
GenericType:   ID '<' TypeArg (',' TypeArg)* '>';                  // map<K,V> list<T> maybe<T> overwrite<T> const<T>
                                                                   // set<T> tree<T> tuple<A,B> range<lo,hi>
                                                                   // enum<a,b,c> object<"pkg.Cls">
ArrayType:     'array' '<' TypeExpr '>' ('[' ShapeDim (',' ShapeDim)* ']')? ('@' STRING)?;   // ShapeDim: INT | '_' | param
StructType:    '{' Field* '}';                                     // anonymous struct = bigraph merge a:T|b:U
LinkType:      'link' '<' '{' Field* '}' ',' '{' Field* '}' '>';
RawType:       STRING;                                             // any bigraph-schema expression verbatim

Let:           DOC* 'let' ID (':' TypeExpr)? '=' Value ';';

InterfaceDecl: DOC* ('process'|'step'|'adapter'|'composite') ID ('at' STRING)? '{'
                 ('config' '{' Field* '}')? ('inputs' FaceBody)? ('outputs' FaceBody)? ('contract' '{' … '}')? '}';
FaceBody:      '{' (PortDecl | CondPorts | '...')* '}' | 'of' 'config' '.' ID ';';   // '...' open face; 'of' delegated
PortDecl:      DOC* ID ':' TypeExpr ('@' STRING)? ';';
CondPorts:     'when' Predicate '{' PortDecl* '}' ('else' '{' PortDecl* '}')?;      // Predicate: config path ('==' Value)?

RootComposite: DOC* 'composite' ID? '{' NodeDecl* '}';
NodeDecl:      StoreDecl | SubtreeDecl | EdgeDecl | ReplicateDecl;
StoreDecl:     DOC* 'store' Key (':' TypeExpr)? ('=' Value)? ';';
SubtreeDecl:   DOC* 'node' Key (':' TypeExpr)? ('=' SiteValue ';' | '{' NodeDecl* '}');
ReplicateDecl: 'replicate' Expr SubtreeDecl;
EdgeDecl:      DOC* ('process'|'step') Key ':' EdgeHead ('every' Expr)? ('priority' INT)? '{' EdgeItem* '}'
             | DOC* 'composite' Key ('every' Expr)? ('at' STRING)? '{' CompositeItem* '}'
             | DOC* 'shared' 'process' Key ':' EdgeHead '{' ('config' ConfigBlock)? '}';
EdgeHead:      [InterfaceDecl] ('at' (STRING | '?' ('(' STRING ')')?))? | 'at' STRING | 'shared' [EdgeDecl];
EdgeItem:      'config' ConfigBlock | 'inputs' WireBlock | 'outputs' WireBlock
             | 'ports' '{' ('inputs' '{' PortDecl* '}')? ('outputs' '{' PortDecl* '}')? '}'
             | 'triggers' '[' Path (',' Path)* ']' | 'extra' '{' KeyValue* '}';
CompositeItem: EdgeItem | 'bridge' '{' ('inputs' WireBlock)? ('outputs' WireBlock)? ('conduits' WireBlock)? '}'
             | 'interface' '{' ('outputs' '{' PortDecl* '}')? '}' | Options | NodeDecl;
ConfigBlock:   '{' (KeyValue (',' KeyValue)* ','?)? '}' | '=' [Let];
WireBlock:     '{' (Wire (',' Wire)* ','?)? '}';     Wire: Key ('->' Path | WireBlock);   // nested = sub-ports
Path:          Seg ('.' Seg)*;     Seg: ID | STRING | '..' | '*' | '[' INT ']';           // fields.A[0][1]

Value:         Literal | Ref | SiteValue | StructLit | MapLit | ListLit | TupleLit | EdgeLit | FileRef | Interp;
SiteValue:     '?' ('(' Value ')')? ('as' (TypeExpr | NamedSort))?;
EdgeLit:       [InterfaceDecl] '{' KeyValue* '}';                  // {address, config} child for higher-order nodes
FileRef:       'file' '(' STRING ')' | 'load' '(' STRING ')';      // text / json|npy|npz|csv; inlined at compile
Expr:          Value | Expr ('*'|'/'|'+'|'-') Expr;                // only in every / replicate / shapes / config leaves
Emit:          'emit' (ID | STRING) '{' Path (',' Path)* '}' ('with' ConfigBlock)? ';';
Options:       'options' '{' KeyValue* '}';     Meta: 'meta' '{' KeyValue* '}';     Key: ID | STRING;

docs.title: 2.3 Rules
docs.text:
• Wire paths are relative to the edge's parent, exactly like the document. The printer uses . and quotes non-identifier keys (node "[0,1]").
  • One Site type; position decides the kind. = ?, = ?(v), = ? as positive (value); at ?, at ?("local:FV") (address, sorted by the interface face); node model : Engine = ?; (model site). An edge whose interface has no at must be written at ?, so openness is visible in review.
  • Literals keep the v1 rules: bare keys make a struct, literal keys make a map, {} is either; - is allowed in numbers; floats need a ..
  • Type spelling: int, bool, float, string, map<string, V>, list<T>, maybe<T>, overwrite<T>, enum<a, b>, array<float>[3,3] @ "uM", { a: T; b: U }, A | B, raw "…". The compiler maps int → integer, bool → boolean, map<string, V> → map[V]. An unknown type name is an error, never passed through.
  • file() / load(): compile inlines the content so the document stays self-contained. The decompiler externalizes strings longer than 2000 characters and arrays with more than 64 elements into sidecar files named <composite>.<path>.{txt,json,npy}.
  • let: module constants inlined at compile. The decompiler hoists subtrees that appear verbatim at two or more places and exceed about ten leaves (a shared grid config, for example), named after the config key.
  • every and replicate accept expressions (every k * dt). The spec projection cannot represent arithmetic.
  • Doc comments: /// on composite → spec description; on param → parameter description; on interface ports → contract description; on stores and edges → text and pblang doc only (never emitted as document keys).
  • emit aliases: parquet, ram, sqlite, xarray, console, json → local:<X>Emitter; an unknown alias is an error listing the known ones. emit "local:ParquetEmitter" { … } gives an address directly.
  • Canonical formatter: two-space indent; the decompiler orders stores, then nodes, then edges, each alphabetically; config entries in interface-declared order, then unknown keys alphabetically; one wire per line when more than two; strings double-quoted.

docs.title: 2.4 Interface files
docs.text:
Generated once per package (<pkg>/pblang/interfaces.pblang), hand-editable for ports the generator cannot see. describe emits what config_schema and interface() report, adds ... and a // TODO: dynamic comment on any face whose inputs()/outputs() body references self.config, and describe --check verifies that a hand-edited file is a superset of the generated one.

module viva_smoldyn;

struct Species { difc: float; count: int = 0; color: string = "black"; display_size: float = 1.0; }

/// Smoldyn particle simulation in a box.
process SmoldynProcess at "local:!viva_smoldyn.processes.SmoldynProcess" {
  config {
    dimensions: int = 3;
    bounds: list<list<float>>;
    boundary_type: string = "r";
    dt: float = 0.01;
    seed: maybe<int>;
    species: map<string, Species>;
    reactions: list<map<string, "any">>;     // raw type kept verbatim: describe found "map"
  }
  inputs { }
  outputs {
    molecule_counts: map<string, int>;
    molecule_positions: list<"any">;
    time: float @ "s";
  }
}

Dynamic ports, written honestly:

module viva_pde_particle;

process SmoldynHybrid at "local:!viva_pde_particle.processes.smoldyn_hybrid.SmoldynHybrid" {
  config { grid: map<string, "any">; config_text: string; particle_species: list<string>;
           field_species: list<string> = []; dt: float = 0.01; step_multiplier: int = 1;
           quiet: bool = true; emit_positions: bool = false; }
  inputs  { fields: map<string, array<float>> @ "uM"; }
  outputs {
    particle_counts: map<string, overwrite<array<float>>>;
    particle_totals: map<string, overwrite<float>>;
    when emit_positions { particle_positions: map<string, overwrite<array<float>>>; }
  }
}

process SpatialRecorder at "local:!viva_pde_particle.processes.recorder.SpatialRecorder" {
  config { out_dir: string; base_dt: float; every: int; layout: map<string, "any">; species: list<string>;
           particle_species: list<string> = []; membranes: map<string, "any"> = {}; region: string = "cell"; }
  inputs {
    when layout.kind == "mesh" { field_dofs: map<string, array<float>>; } else { fields: map<string, array<float>>; }
    when particle_species { particle_positions: map<string, array<float>>; }
    ...                                   // open face: undeclared ports warn, not error
  }
  outputs { }
}

/// Runs a child process on a sub-multiple of the base tick.
process Stepper at "local:!viva_pde_particle.processes.stepper.Stepper" {
  config { process: edge; dt: float; every: int = 1; phase: int = 0; }   // `edge` = an {address, config} child
  inputs  of config.process;
  outputs of config.process;
}

adapter GridCountsToConcentration at "local:!viva_pde_particle.steps.transfer.GridCountsToConcentration" {
  config  { grid: map<string, "any">; species: list<string>; staircase: map<string, "any"> = {}; }
  inputs  { particle_counts: map<string, array<float>> @ "count"; }
  outputs { particle_conc:   map<string, overwrite<array<float>>> @ "uM"; }
}

adapter is step plus role metadata; the checker uses it for unit-mismatch fix hints. The DSL-only edge type is an {address, config} child spec; in config position it is written as an edge literal (SmoldynHybrid { … }).

docs.title: 4.1 viva-smoldyn reversible dimerization (from reversible-dimerization.composite.yaml)
docs.text:
module viva_smoldyn.composites.reversible_dimerization;
import viva_smoldyn.{SmoldynProcess};

meta { tags = ["particles", "reaction-diffusion", "3d", "simularium"] }

/// Smoldyn 3D reversible dimerization: fast red monomers A diffuse and bind pairwise into
/// slower blue dimers B (A + A <-> B) in a reflecting cubic box. Emits per-species counts,
/// per-molecule positions, and time each step; the positions drive a Simularium trajectory.
composite reversible_dimerization {
  store molecule_counts: map<string, int> = {};
  store molecule_positions: list<"any"> = [];
  store time: float = 0.0;

  process smoldyn : SmoldynProcess every 0.5 {
    config {
      dimensions = 3,
      bounds = [[0, 50], [0, 50], [0, 50]],
      boundary_type = "r",
      dt = 0.01,
      seed = 12345,
      species = {
        "A" = { difc = 3.0, count = 250, color = "red",  display_size = 1.2 },
        "B" = { difc = 1.0, count = 0,   color = "blue", display_size = 2.0 }
      },
      reactions = [ { "name" = "dimerize", "subs" = ["A", "A"], "prds" = ["B"], "rate" = 2.0, "kb" = 0.15 } ]
    }
    inputs  { }
    outputs { molecule_counts -> molecule_counts, molecule_positions -> molecule_positions, time -> time }
  }
}

emit parquet { molecule_counts, molecule_positions, time };

pblang compile --to yaml reproduces the yaml (requires computed from the import, name from the composite); pblang compile produces the document with the emitter step materialized. From the yaml alone the stores are untyped (molecule_counts: {}); the checker reports W-STORE-UNTYPED with the fix "declare : map<string, int> (from SmoldynProcess.outputs.molecule_counts)". That review signal is exactly what the DSL is for.

docs.title: 4.2 Nested growth-division composite (local:Composite with a bridge)
docs.text:
import demo.{Grow, Divide};

param growth_rate: float = 0.1;

composite grow_divide {
  store environment: map<string, float> = { "nutrient" = 10.0 };
  store mass_out: float = 0.0;

  /// One cell as a nested composite; the bridge exposes its mass and a division signal.
  composite cell every 1.0 {
    store mass: float = 1.0;
    store divide_signal: bool = false;
    process grow : Grow every 1.0 {
      config  { rate = growth_rate }
      inputs  { mass -> mass, env -> ../environment }   // `..` escapes the inner root through the bridge
      outputs { mass -> mass }
    }
    step divide : Divide {
      config  { threshold = 2.0 }
      inputs  { mass -> mass }
      outputs { divide -> divide_signal }
    }

    bridge {
      inputs   { environment -> environment }           // inner path for the outer `environment` port
      outputs  { mass -> mass }
      conduits { divide -> divide_signal }
    }
    interface { outputs { mass: float; } }
    options { run_steps_on_init = true }

    inputs  { environment -> environment }              // outer wires, relative to the root
    outputs { mass -> mass_out }
  }
}

Compiles to cell: {_type: process, address: "local:Composite", interval: 1.0, config: {schema, state, bridge: {inputs: {environment: ["environment"]}, outputs: {mass: ["mass"]}, conduits: {divide: ["divide_signal"]}}, interface: {outputs: {mass: "float"}}, run_steps_on_init: true}, inputs, outputs}. Decompiling a saved document whose nested config.state is empty raises W-NESTED-SAVE-LOSSY.

docs.title: 4.3 viva-pde-particle hybrid (FV PDE + Smoldyn + adapters + Stepper + SpatialRecorder)
docs.text:
module viva_pde_particle.composites.hybrid;
import viva_pde_particle.{FVReactionDiffusion, SmoldynHybrid, GridCountsToConcentration,
                          ExtendGridField, Stepper, SpatialRecorder};

param dt: float = 0.01;
param step_multiplier: int = 5;
/// Which PDE engine fills the `pde` slot; the face is shared by FV and FEniCSx.
param pde_engine: string = "fv" choices ["fv", "fenicsx"];

let grid = { "origin" = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0], "size" = [10.0, 10.0, 10.0], "num" = [20, 20, 20] };
let species = ["A", "B"];

composite hybrid {
  store fields:          map<string, array<float>[20,20,20] @ "uM">    = load("hybrid.fields.npz");
  store particle_counts: map<string, array<float>[20,20,20] @ "count"> = load("hybrid.particle_counts.npz");
  store particle_conc:   map<string, array<float>[20,20,20] @ "uM">    = load("hybrid.particle_conc.npz");
  store particle_totals: map<string, float> = { "A" = 1200.0, "B" = 0.0 };
  store fields_ext:      map<string, array<float>>;

  /// Filled by the builder with the engine chosen by `pde_engine`; both engines satisfy this face.
  process pde : FVReactionDiffusion at ?("local:FVReactionDiffusion") every dt {
    config  { grid = grid, pde = load("hybrid.pde.json"), dt = dt,
              domain = { "mask" = ?, "volume_fraction" = ? } }    // builder-computed arrays left open
    inputs  { fields -> fields, external_conc -> particle_conc }
    outputs { fields -> fields }
  }

  step particle_to_field : GridCountsToConcentration {
    config  { grid = grid, species = species }
    inputs  { particle_counts -> particle_counts }
    outputs { particle_conc -> particle_conc }
  }

  step extend_field : ExtendGridField {
    config  { grid = grid, species = species, staircase = {} }
    inputs  { fields -> fields }
    outputs { fields_ext -> fields_ext }
  }

  /// SmoldynHybrid driven on a sub-multiple of dt, phase k-1 (vcell-fvsolver coupling).
  process particles : Stepper every dt {
    config {
      process = SmoldynHybrid {                                  // edge literal: {address, config}
        grid = grid, config_text = file("hybrid.particles.smol"),
        particle_species = species, field_species = ["A"],
        dt = dt, step_multiplier = step_multiplier
      },
      dt = dt, every = step_multiplier, phase = step_multiplier - 1
    }
    inputs  { fields -> fields }                                 // face delegated from config.process
    outputs { particle_counts -> particle_counts, particle_totals -> particle_totals }
  }

  process recorder : SpatialRecorder every dt {
    config  { out_dir = "${out_dir}", base_dt = dt, every = 10,
              layout = { "kind" = "grid", "grid" = grid }, species = species }
    inputs  { fields -> fields }                                 // ok: `when layout.kind == "mesh"` is false
  }
}

load() and file() keep the text reviewable while the document stays self-contained; the ? inside domain are config sites the builder fills with fill_sites; the Stepper child is an edge literal, which the checker uses to resolve the delegated face and to type-check the child's config; pde_engine is a plain spec parameter (the mapping to an address stays in the builder; the DSL records the open address site with its default). phase = step_multiplier - 1 is an expression: the spec projection reports E-SPEC-EXPR, the template projection evaluates it from the defaults with W-PARAM-EVALUATED.

docs.title: 4.4 spatio-flux cell "[0,1]" with array-indexed wires
docs.text:
import spatio_flux.{DynamicFBA};
import spatio_flux.types;                 // registers positive_float etc. (register_types hook)

param n_bins: int = 2;

composite spatial_dfba {
  store fields: map<string, array<float>[n_bins, n_bins] @ "mM"> = {
    "glucose" = [[10.0, 10.0], [10.0, 10.0]], "acetate" = [[0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0]], "biomass" = [[0.1, 0.1], [0.1, 0.1]]
  };

  node "[0,1]" {
    process dfba : DynamicFBA every 1.0 {
      config { model_file = "textbook", biomass_identifier = "biomass",
               kinetic_params = { "glucose" = [0.5, 1.0], "acetate" = [0.5, 2.0] },
               substrate_update_reactions = { "glucose" = "EX_glc__D_e", "acetate" = "EX_ac_e" },
               bounds = { "EX_o2_e" = { "lower" = -2.0, "upper" = ? as maybe<float> },
                          "ATPM" = { "lower" = 1.0, "upper" = 1.0 } } }
      inputs  { substrates { glucose -> ../fields.glucose[0][1], acetate -> ../fields.acetate[0][1],
                             biomass -> ../fields.biomass[0][1] } }
      outputs { substrates { glucose -> ../fields.glucose[0][1], acetate -> ../fields.acetate[0][1],
                             biomass -> ../fields.biomass[0][1] } }
    }
  }
}

../fields.glucose[0][1] → ["..","fields","glucose",0,1]. The checker resolves the path type through map → array → index → index and checks it against the port type with core.resolve_schemas. n_bins in a shape is a param, so the shape is [2,2] in both projections (shapes must be ground at compile time).

docs.title: 4.5 Template with a face site for the engine and a required param
docs.text:
import viva_pde_particle.{PdeEngine};    // an interface: a process declaration with no `at`

param n_particles: int = ?;              // required: fill_sites must supply it
param dt: float = 0.01;

composite pde_study {
  store fields: map<string, array<float>> = {};
  node model : PdeEngine = ?;            // model site: a whole subtree admitted by the PdeEngine face
  process engine : PdeEngine at ? every dt {   // address site sorted by the face
    config  { n = n_particles }
    inputs  { fields -> fields }
    outputs { fields -> fields }
  }
}

Compiles in template mode to sites at engine/address (sorted by the link face), engine/config/n (required), interval (default 0.01) and model. pblang check reports groundness with process-bigraph's own wording: required site(s) left unfilled: 'engine/config/n', 'engine/address', 'model'.

Where the checks run. The checker is TypeScript (dsl/src/language/v2/check.ts), inside the Langium services: the same code produces editor diagnostics, the browser's diagnostics (the language server runs in a web worker) and the CLI's check --json envelope. Its inputs are data only: the parsed document and header manifests (JSON). Units use mathjs. Python calls the CLI (process_bigraph_lang/v2/check.py), which cli-native provides without Node or Deno at run time (Deno compiles it once when the wheel is built). There is one grammar and one checker; the compliance suite is dsl/test/v2/check.test.ts, mirrored by the Python tests through the CLI.

Editor services. Hover and completion are built on the same resolution the checker uses (dsl/src/language/v2/resolve.ts: which header an edge is declared by, and how a path walks the composite tree). Hover shows an edge's header as a header file would print it, a port's declared type and the store it is wired to, the store or node a path segment names, a header's config field under a config key, and the declarations of stores, params, models and emitter aliases, with their /// docs. Completion offers the header's unwired ports in inputs { } / outputs { }, its config fields in config { } (required first, key = inserted), the stores and nodes of the edge's parent in a wire path and the keys below a dict store, the emitter aliases after emit, and interfaces at process x : from the registry and from header files open in the workspace, with the import they need added as an additional edit. The keywords a key may coincide with (every, process, ...) are not proposed in key positions. In the editor, header .pblang files in the workspace answer import a.b.{X} directly (a document with module a.b; declaring X is local:!a.b.X), so a composite next to its generated headers is checked without a manifest; the CLI takes manifests with --interfaces.

Compile and decompile. The reader (document or CompositeSpec -> model), the writer (model -> document or CompositeSpec), the printer (model -> text) and the binder (Langium AST -> model) are TypeScript too (dsl/src/language/v2/{reader,writer,printer,bind}.ts over the model in model.ts), so cli-native compile and cli-native decompile are the only implementations: the same code serves the CLI, the editor and the browser. Documents cross the CLI boundary as JSON in bigraph_schema.json_codec's encoding (numpy arrays tagged; tuples tagged as __tuple__ by the Python side), with ints and floats kept apart (1 is not 1.0), dicts in source order, and Python's float and string spellings reproduced so that printed text and sidecar assets are byte-identical on both sides. compile runs the checker first and stops on errors (--strict makes warnings fatal; --force compiles an existing document that relies on defaults the checker flags). headers renders a manifest as .pblang header files, model-header renders describe-model's JSON, graph prints the wiring graph for viewers.

The Python API. process_bigraph_lang.v2 exposes compile_text / compile_file and decompile, thin wrappers over those commands, plus what has to be Python: describe_module (introspection runs where the classes import; it writes the manifest the CLI reads), describe_sbml (the model header as JSON), and the normalizer (equivalent, diff_documents; it needs bigraph-schema's core.render). There is no Python model of a composite. This is deliberate: a Python tool that builds composites targets the DSL text, where the result is checked, reviewed and documented, rather than a Python object model that would be a second authoring surface. A builder in viva-pde-particle, for example, emits .pblang text (or a document it then decompiles) and compiles that.
