docs.text:
• vivarium-workbench: consume manifest.json for installed packages (fall back to stage A inside env_worker for unpublished workspace packages, so there is one registry model); RegistryProcess gains manifest_ref, dynamic_ports, port_semantics, adapter, fingerprint; published/introspected/stale badges; a workflow view hosting the existing Monaco and Langium worker plus a diagnostics panel; parameter forms from compile --to yaml.
  • viva-catalog: modules.json gains manifest_path; nightly ecosystem-interfaces.json and components.json; hosts the reusable workflow.
  • viva-superpowers: /viva-compose, /viva-publish-interfaces, /viva-adapt; docs/conventions/interfaces.md; composites.md documents requires.packages and the generated-file header.
  • pbg-template: scaffold pblang/, the override stub, the workflow and schema references.
  • Upstream asks (process-bigraph, bigraph-schema): python -m process_bigraph.describe (adopt stage A), Edge.port_semantics(), an Edge.adapter marker, Edge.ports_depend_on, JSON-safe ProcessContract.to_dict(), find_candidates over manifests, CompositeSpec requires.packages, core.access(strict=True), bigraph-schema#188, process-bigraph#213.
  • This repo: process_bigraph_lang/registry/ (manifest models, resolver, search, render, stage B), process_bigraph_lang/check/ (diagnostics model, checks, preflight), process_bigraph_lang/cli.py (pblang), packages/pblang-describe/, docs/schemas/*.json, docs/vocab/faces.json.

docs.title: 7. Roadmap
docs.text:
Phase Scope Validation 1 design docs and the round-trip prototype in this repo (see the plan) corpus round-trips; snapshots reviewed 2 DSL v2 grammar (Langium), compile/decompile/doc/check CLI, lock, LSP forwarding of Python diagnostics round-trip viva-smoldyn and viva-vcell-fvsolver yamls; compiled documents run under Composite 3 publish real interfaces: viva-pde-particle (overrides for Stepper, SplittingCoordinator, SmoldynHybrid; adapter metadata on the transfer steps), viva-smoldyn, viva-emitters; catalog aggregation and reusable workflow; pbg-template scaffold the catalog serves ports; registry search --face finds the grid-counts → mesh adapter; verify green in CI 4 authoring loop and workbench integration the pde-particle hybrid rebuilt from DSL via the skill with no hand-edited yaml runs in the workbench; error-UX review against the pain-point list 5 execution without one env: environment, preflight --suggest-env, --exec-plan rest with compose-api the hybrid runs with Smoldyn in a separate container; preflight catches a deliberately stale interface 6 upstreaming and hardening describe, markers and strict access land upstream; heuristics leave stage A

Risks: bigraph-schema version skew (the toolchain floor must be ≥ 1.7 for matching and audit_contract; feature-detect); dynamic ports are a long tail (override files are the escape hatch; check degrades to hints, never silence); custom Node types with Python apply behaviour cannot be data (validate loosely and say so); TypeScript and Python validators drifting (a shared fixture corpus run by both suites); generated-file drift (verify gates on both sides).

docs.title: v2 background: research notes (2026-10-11)
docs.text:
This page records what was learned while taking a second look at the language, a year after its first design. It is the evidence behind the v2 language design, the registry and authoring design and the implementation plan.

Sources were the local clones of process-bigraph (1.8.5, commit e5325c1), bigraph-schema (1.6.0, commit 8268aa1; origin is at 1.7.0), the viva-* and pbg-* packages, vivarium-workbench, viva-catalog (read through the GitHub API), and this repository. The Python environment of this repository has process-bigraph 1.8.4 and bigraph-schema 1.6.0.

docs.title: 1. What motivated the second look
docs.text:
• process-bigraph grew templates and sites (open holes in a document, filled later), contracts and contract audits, and a declarative CompositeSpec (*.composite.yaml).
  • The ecosystem grew to about fifty viva-* packages, a browser workbench, a nascent registry and prompt-driven authoring tools.
  • viva-pde-particle, a co-simulation of a PDE solver and a Brownian-dynamics particle solver, shows what real composites need and what today's language cannot say.
  • The current DSL is one-directional, lossy, and was designed as the document a person writes by hand. The new framing is different: the DSL is a verifiable target layer. End users author with prompt-guided tools against a declared registry of components; the DSL is where the result is type-checked, audited, documented and explained, and from which the runnable document is generated.

docs.title: 2.1 Composite document
docs.text:
A document is {"schema": …, "state": …} plus optional top-level options. Composite.config_schema declares schema, state, interface{inputs,outputs}, bridge{inputs,outputs} (and an undeclared bridge.conduits), global_time_precision, run_steps_on_init, parallel_steps, parallel_processes, parallel_workers, skip_process_state and (clone only) contract_strict. initialize injects global_time at the root.

An edge node in state may carry:

Key Notes _type process, step or link; may be omitted in state when schema declares it address "protocol:data" string or {"protocol","data"} dict; no protocol means local config realized against the class config_schema inputs / outputs wires: list paths relative to the edge's parent; a string is a one-element path; nested dicts wire sub-ports; .. goes up; * is a star jump _inputs / _outputs port-schema overrides merged with interface() interval process only, must be > 0, default 1.0 priority, _triggers step only any other non-_ key realized as extra data

Address protocols: local:Name (registry lookup; discovery registers both module.Class and a short alias, first one wins), local:!module.Class (import by dotted path, portable), parallel:, ray:, rest: and git: (allow-listed repo at a SHA, per-SHA venv, subprocess RPC, face-conformance check). registry_dependent_addresses and assert_portable_addresses in bigraph_schema/protocols.py lint for the non-portable form.

Nested composites are a process at local:Composite whose config holds state, schema, bridge and interface; the outer ports derive from bridge. Saving such a document is lossy: the inner state comes back empty (observed on 1.8.4 and the clone). Shared processes use shared_process plus shared_process_ref.

Emitters are steps whose config has emit: <schema>; viva-emitters provides RAM, sqlite, parquet and xarray. CompositeSpec has emitters: [{address, paths}] sugar, materialized by process_bigraph.emitter.emitter_node_from_declaration.

docs.title: 2.2 Serialized documents differ from authored ones
docs.text:
Composite.save() writes {"state": serialize_state(), "schema": serialize_schema()}. Compared with the authoring document:

  • _type appears only in the schema half; the state half has dict addresses {"protocol","data"}.
  • config is fully defaulted; _inputs/_outputs are always present, often in compact string form ("level:float"); a _contract block is added.
  • global_time and process-contributed stores (an emitter's results) are added.
  • The schema half is rendered without defaults, so a dict schema collapses to a string ("pt": "x:float|y:float") and store defaults are lost (float{3.5} becomes float).
  • Rendering quirks: map[string,float] becomes map[float]; array[float] becomes array[1,float].
  • Reloading {"state": saved_state} alone silently loses every process; both halves are needed.

docs.title: 2.3 Templates and sites
docs.text:
The vocabulary is site, sort, admits, face, fill, compose, ground, template. "Slot" was an earlier draft name and was dropped deliberately. There is one Site type (bigraph_schema/schema.py, class Site(Empty) with _sort and the inherited _default); its kind is decided by its sort and position:

Kind Written as Admits value site {"_type":"site","_sort":"float"} core.check(sort, filler) face site _sort is link[in,out] or {"_type":"link","_inputs","_outputs"} face_conforms: every required port, resolvable types; extras ok address site "address": {"_type":"site","_sort": FACE} inside an edge node filler is an address; face from the registered class config site a site anywhere under an edge's config as a value site named sort _sort: "results" via core.register_sort or a contract name custom admits function unsorted "site" anything

{"_control":"replicate","_count":N} expands a region N times (assembly.build only). The algebra is in bigraph_schema/assembly.py (interfaces, is_ground, admits_why, face_conforms, fill_sites, replicate, build); the process-bigraph layer is process_bigraph/templates.py (open_sites, required_open_sites, is_ground_document, fill_template, template_document, load_template, save_template). bigraph-schema 1.7 adds bigraph_schema.matching.find_candidates(core, site).

Fill semantics: bindings are keyed by bare site key (when unique) or by /-joined path; an unbound site with a _default is filled from it; a value filler becomes the sort with _default=value; template_document renders with defaults=True (without it, values are lost). Composite.initialize checks groundness before realization (clone) and raises composite document is not ground — required site(s) left unfilled: '…'. Two upstream traps remain: a schema entry used to swallow a state site (process-bigraph#213), and address sites can only be filled with names registered through core.register_link (bigraph-schema#188).

docs.title: 2.4 Type system
docs.text:
String grammar (bigraph_schema/parse.py): name[params]{default}, struct a:T|b:U, union A~B, parentheses. Builtins: node, atom, empty, union, tuple, boolean, integer, float, float64, nonnegative, complex, range, string, enum, maybe, overwrite, const, quote, list, set, map, tree, array, dataframe, path, wires, protocol, schema, link, object, function, quantity, site, inner_name, outer_name, face; process-bigraph adds step, process, composite, interface, bridge, shared_process, interval. Dict forms use _element, _key, _value, _values, _options, _shape, _data, _units, _bits, _min, _max, _sort, _inputs, _outputs, _class, _default, _inherit.

Two traps: any is not a type and an unknown string name passes through core.access silently, so typos are not caught; and a plain map[array[float]] output is additive unless wrapped in overwrite[...], which silently changes update semantics. Custom types are registered via a register_types(core) hook and get behaviour from plum dispatch methods, not from _apply keys (those no longer exist).

docs.title: 2.5 Interfaces and discovery
docs.text:
Edge (bigraph_schema/edge.py) has class attributes config_schema, description, contract and instance methods inputs(), outputs(), interface(), describe(). ProcessContract (bigraph_schema/contract.py) is a structured face with _units, _min, _max, description, assumptions and references; audit_contract and completeness (1.7) grade it. DraftProcess declares ports and a contract with no dynamics.

Discovery is import-based everywhere: allocate_core() scans every installed distribution that depends on bigraph-schema and imports it (with a lazy on-disk name→module index); import errors in submodules are swallowed. There is no static interface manifest and no entry-point mechanism. The REST server exposes /list-processes and /process/{p}/config-schema.

docs.title: 3.1 viva-pde-particle
docs.text:
Pipeline: model input (Python HybridModel dataclasses or SBML Spatial via libvcell) → partition() into PDE and particle halves → Smoldyn config text → geometry (vcell-fenics GeometryDescription realized by Netgen or libvcell; derived mesh, membrane triangles, volume samples, fold maps) → engines (FV, FEniCSx Q1/P1, SmoldynHybrid) → coupling (adapter steps both ways; timing by Jacobi scheduling, Stepper with every/phase, or SplittingCoordinator) → output (HybridTrajectory from a Python run loop, or SpatialRecorder writing a zarr bundle; SpatialExport after the run because there is no end-of-run hook) → visualization (viz3d).

Declarations: config schemas are mostly untyped "map" blobs (grid, pde partition, mesh spec, domain arrays, generated config_text); ports are always map[array[float]] in and map[overwrite[array[float]]] out; no custom types, shapes or units (these live in prose in docs/DESIGN.md §13). Ports depend on config (SmoldynHybrid adds particle_positions only if emit_positions; SpatialRecorder.inputs() depends on layout.kind) or on children (Stepper.inputs() returns its child's; SplittingCoordinator unions its children's ports). Adapters are steps in steps/transfer.py with config {grid: map, mesh: map, species: list[string]}.

Composites are built only by Python functions in composites/hybrid.py, wrapped by @composite_generator in composites/examples.py; there are no *.composite.yaml files. Builder logic that is not declarative today: engine choice by name, adapter choice, conditional wiring, option-combination validation, pre-computing initial arrays by instantiating steps (steps don't run at init), a probe process to learn the DOF count, seeded particle placement, generating the Smoldyn text, and keeping grid/mesh/species consistent across components. Addresses are bare local:Name registered by a hand-written build_core() because editable installs are not discovered. The package runs in a single pixi environment (dolfinx, gmsh, a patched Smoldyn submodule, pyvcell) on linux-64 and osx-arm64, with a compose-api Docker image.

docs.title: 3.2 Other packages
docs.text:
Package Declarations and authoring viva-smoldyn, viva-vcell-fvsolver declarative *.composite.yaml (CompositeSpec: requires, parameters with ${} substitution, emitters) viva-fenics @composite_generator dict literals that compute initial mesh arrays in Python; one custom type fem_field viva-emitters emitters as steps with emit: schema; the only self-describing contract (EmitterContract(output_kind, output_uri_config_key)) viva-uq injects parameters at "a/b/c" paths; builds an emitter class at runtime to dodge type checking spatio-flux (older) richest custom types (positive_float with custom apply, enum, maybe, map[reaction]); one DynamicFBA per grid cell with array-indexed wires ["..","fields",mol,i,j]; port shapes computed from config pbg-ptools workbench viewer plugin, no processes

Nothing publishes process interfaces as data. The only entry-point group is process_bigraph.spec_generators for composite generators. The catalog/modules.json in viva-superpowers lists repo pointers, not interfaces. pbg-template scaffolds a workspace (JSON Schemas for workspace.yaml, study and investigation; a core.py stub).

docs.title: 3.3 vivarium-workbench and loom
docs.text:
The workbench is a local FastAPI server that turns a workspace directory (workspace.yaml, composites/*.composite.yaml, studies, investigations; every mutation committed to git) into an interactive notebook. It never imports workspace code in the HTTP process; a stdlib-only env_worker.py runs in the workspace interpreter, imports <package>.core.build_core(), walks core.link_registry, reads config_schema and calls inputs()/outputs() with the class standing in for self (ports are None when that fails). The record sent to the frontend is RegistryProcess {name, address, kind, schema_preview, aliases, source, description, config_schema, inputs, outputs} plus, on GitHub, contract_audit. Composites are authored as yaml with parameter forms (ParameterDecl {type, default, description, choices}), dotted-path "perturb" overrides, per-process "try it", and the viva-superpowers skills. Validation: JSON Schema at save time, {error} envelopes, build errors as a warning chip with the stringified exception, a preflight that aggregates silent failures, and (on GitHub) a composite-level contract audit with codes wire-type-mismatch, wire-unit-mismatch, unknown_port. Runs are local (SQLite results) or remote via viva-api.

bigraph-loom is archived and vendored at vivarium_workbench/loom/: a read-only React Flow viewer and inspector with many layout engines, drill-down into composite processes, a contract panel and a raw JSON panel. It has no text pretty-printer, no diffs, no templates and no validation. Its process node model is {processType, address, config, configSchema, interval, inputPorts, outputPorts, inputSchema, outputSchema, contract, isCompositeProcess} with wires resolved to absolute store paths in convert.ts.

docs.title: 3.4 viva-catalog
docs.text: "Ledger for the vivarium ecosystem": modules.json lists repos tagged with the GitHub topic viva-marketplace ({name, source, ref, package, homepage, description, tags}); a nightly workflow shallow-clones each one and AST-scans class names into ecosystem-index.json (processes: [{name, description}], steps, composites, studies, investigations). There are no ports, config schemas or addresses in the index. A PR proposing AST-extracted ports, JSON Schemas and a marketplace_info.get_info() hook was closed unmerged on 2026-07-30. Published at vivarium-collective.github.io/viva-catalog/*.json and consumed by the workbench marketplace tab.

docs.title: 3.5 Pain points collected
docs.text:
1. A missing address fails late and cryptically: no link found at address: {'protocol': 'local', 'data': 'X'}.
  2. Unknown type names (int, any) are accepted silently.
  3. Additive vs overwrite[...] update semantics are silently wrong; an empty-array initial store is replaced rather than added to.
  4. Remote failures succeed silently: dropped process swaps, typo'd emit paths that materialize empty dicts, empty variant grids.
  5. ${param} substitution leaves malformed references as-is; values may arrive as strings.
  6. Discovery swallows ImportErrors; a registry cache can be stale and show none of the workspace's own processes.
  7. Float-sum interval drift defers updates.
  8. Validation lives in initialize()/update() as ValueErrors, not in schemas.
  9. Schemas for emitters, studies and investigations are hand-mirrored across repos and unversioned.
  10. Missing observables are returned as 0.0.
  11. Saved nested composites lose their inner state.

docs.title: 4. This repository before v2
docs.text:
• One direction only: DSL → document. No printer, formatter, decompiler, hover or completion provider. dsl/src/language/sbml.ts is a narrow precedent for generating DSL from external data.
  • Lossy compile: aliases erased, struct-typed stores split per field, references inlined, remote type names dropped, units and comments dropped, interval never set.
  • Missing constructs compared with the 1.x document: emitters, interval, nested composites and bridge, maps of edges, custom types with apply behaviour, enum/union/maybe/optional, array dtype and shape, imports across files, doc comments, protocol-aware addresses, units on types, nested or per-key wiring, .. paths, remote-typed config values, expressions.
  • The old ANTLR grammar (antlr/pblang.g4) had different ideas worth remembering: parameters with units, update expressions, maybe[T], store hierarchies, composite_def, an sbml block.

docs.title: SED-ML plan: models described in SED-ML, run as checked .pblang templates on several solvers
docs.text:
Status: agreed 2026-10-12. This is the language half of compose-api's docs/plan-sedml.md, which holds the decisions, the service side (runs, datasets, comparisons, sources, suites) and the phase table. Each PR here updates the status below.

Step What State 1a sedml.py: SED-ML read with the standard library into pblang-sedml/0 JSON, with an unsupported[] list in review 1b The role and adapter declarations (TimeCourseSolver, the SED-ML adapters' faces) in review 1c The template printer: one .pblang composite per SED-ML task, the solver an open address site in review 1d One instance per solver, checked and compiled against that solver's environment manifest; refusal findings in review 1e SED-ML plots as Plotly figures in review 1f CLI sedml describe and sedml translate; corpus and snapshots; release 0.3.0 in review (release to come)

docs.title: Why here
docs.text:
compose-api will run SED-ML models (curated BioModels entries, biosimulations.org projects, uploads) as process-bigraph documents, one run per solver, and compare the results. The translation lives in this package, not in the service, for the reason CLAUDE.md gives: there is no Python model of a composite, and nothing runnable skips the checker. A SED-ML task becomes .pblang text; the solver is an open site; filling it with a solver is checked against that solver's interface in the environment that runs it. The same template, filled with each solver in turn, is the "same workflow on several implementations" that the comparison needs, and the text is what the composite viewer shows and "Edit a copy" opens.

It also exercises two parts of the language that no real workload uses yet: model headers (describe-model, model X from "file", design section 5.6) and templates with address sites (design section 4.5).

docs.title: Scope, version 1
docs.text:
Read: uniform time course simulations (initial time, output start and end, number of points, the KiSAO algorithm and its parameters); tasks; models with attribute changes (changeAttribute on an SBML target by XPath, resolved to the SBML id); simple data generators (one variable, a time symbol or an SBML id by XPath, with math that is the variable itself or the variable times a constant); reports (data set id, label, data generator); plots (2D curves: x and y data generators, names, log scales; 3D surfaces).

Reported, never dropped silently (an unsupported[] entry with the element's id and why): steady state and one-step simulations, repeated and nested tasks, other change kinds (computeChange, addXML, removeXML, changeXML), data generators with other math, models that are not SBML, references to remote models.

docs.title: Settled in 1a
docs.text:
• Simple data generators are linear combinations: x, c * x, x / c, x + y, x - y, with constants from <cn> or the data generator's own parameters. The Ciliberto project needs the sum (Swe1T is four species added). Each is terms: [{variable, coefficient}].
  • Steps, not points. L1V1-3's numberOfPoints and L1V4's numberOfSteps both count intervals; the description says number_of_steps, and a time course has number_of_steps + 1 points.
  • An archive's SED-ML is what its manifest.xml declares with the SED-ML format (the master first), else every *.sedml member.
  • Targets resolve to {kind, id, attribute} for species, parameters, compartments and reactions (a reaction's variable is its rate). A data generator may name any of them: BIOMD0000000012's report asks for all four kinds, so a solver that returns only species leaves the rest unfilled. Phase 2 (the adapters) must say which kinds each solver provides, and the compile step reports the gap per solver.
  • Algorithms are KiSAO terms, sometimes generic: BIOMD0000000012 asks for KISAO:0000694 ("ODE solver"), not a specific integrator. Matching a solver to an algorithm (1d) uses the KiSAO hierarchy, not equality.

docs.title: What a task becomes (as built in 1b to 1f)
docs.text:
process_bigraph_lang/v2/sedml_translate.py. Each task of each SED-ML file becomes a composite of four steps (see tests/fixtures/data/v2/sedml/snapshots/ for the repressilator's template and COPASI instance, and the Ciliberto project's Tellurium instance):

composite task_1 {
  store result: numeric_result = {};
  store data: map<string, list<float>> = {};

  step simulate : TelluriumUTCStep {                 // the template says `TimeCourseSolver at ?`
    config { model_source = "BIOMD0000000297_url.changed.xml", time = 140.0, n_points = 201,
             output_dir = "/experiment/output" }
    outputs { result -> result }
  }
  step observe : DataGenerators { config { generators = {...}, constants = {...}, skip = 0 } ... }
  step report : Report { config { output_dir = ..., reports = {...} } inputs { data -> data } }
  step plots : Plots { config { output_dir = ..., plots = {...} } inputs { data -> data } }
}

Decided while building it (2026-10-13):

  • The role is the generic solvers' common face. pbsim-common's CopasiUTCStep and TelluriumUTCStep declare the same interface in registry_env's manifest: config model_source, time, n_points, output_dir, the species inputs, result: numeric_result. TimeCourseSolver is that face; no wrappers are needed.
  • Filling a solver is printing it, and the checker is the face check. Process-bigraph 1.0.5 (registry_env) has no sites, so a run's document must be ground. The template keeps simulate : TimeCourseSolver at ? (it checks with only I300); an instance imports the solver's own class and names it, so the existing checker verifies its config and ports against the environment's manifest (S021, S022, T121, W200). A solver that does not fit is refused by those findings, with no new language machinery.
  • Model changes are applied at translation (Jim, 2026-10-13): they are constants, and the generic solvers read the model from config, which no step can change. The instance reads <model>.changed.xml, written with the change applied (namespaces kept), and its meta lists each change.
  • Adapters live in a new package we own (Jim, 2026-10-13): biosim-toolkit (biosim_toolkit.sedml), a rollup of trusted utilities (SED-ML, model and format adapters, reports, data, visualization). Each generated file declares them inline at their addresses, so it is self-contained.
  • The output grid. The generic solvers start at 0 and take points, not steps: time is the output end, n_points covers the initial time to the end on the output's step, and observe drops the skip points before the output start. An initial time other than 0 (X402) or an output that is not on that grid (X403) refuses the task.
  • What a solver returns. The generic steps return species columns and time. Data generators reading constant parameters or compartments take their values (after changes) from the model header; those reading rule-defined parameters or reaction rates are left out of that solver's reports and plots (X404, one finding per kind).
  • Algorithms. A solver lists the KiSAO terms it implements (default first). The generic KISAO:0000694, a listed term, or an ancestor of the solver's default is accepted; another ODE algorithm is a substitution (X405, a warning: COPASI runs LSODA/LSODAR where CVODE is asked for); anything else refuses (X406). The ODE terms and their ancestors are kisao_ode.json, from the KiSAO ontology.
  • Plots are built at run time. The Plots adapter takes each SED-ML plot's curves (data generator ids, names, log axes) in its config and writes the Plotly figure with the data; no template files and no fill_plot. The comparison page overlays the figures of several runs.
  • The data store is overwrite<map<string, list<float>>>: bigraph-schema 1.0's map apply keeps only keys the store already has, so a map store would stay empty (found running the chain under registry_env's versions).
  • One archive per task and solver: pbest runs the first top-level .pbg, so instance_archive holds one compiled document (<task>.pbg), its text and the model files.
  • No browser translation. The web app previews a translation through compose-api, which calls this package.

docs.title: Findings
docs.text: Code Severity Meaning X400 warning a SED-ML element version 1 does not translate (from describe's unsupported) X401 error a change or data generator names an element the model does not have, or the model file is missing X402 error the time course does not start at 0, where the generic solvers start X403 error the output is not on a grid from the initial time X404 warning data generators read values the solver does not return; they are left out of its outputs X405 warning the solver runs a different ODE algorithm than the one asked for X406 error the solver implements no algorithm of the kind asked for

docs.title: Interfaces
docs.text:
• Python: describe_sedml(path) -> SedmlDescription (pblang-sedml/0); translate(path, solvers, output_dir) -> Translation (per task: the template, one instance per accepted solver, the model files, the findings); compile_instance(task, solver, manifests, addresses="registered"); instance_archive(task, solver, document) -> bytes; solvers_from(data) for compose-api's solvers.yaml.
  • CLI: python -m process_bigraph_lang.v2 sedml describe x.omex [-o d.json]; sedml translate x.omex --solvers solvers.yaml -i env.json -o dir/ (texts, models, one archive per task and solver, findings.json). compile --addresses registered writes local:module.Class (the CLI now has the option the TypeScript API had).
